title: Full-Body Power
intro: A full gym session built around the back squat, with jumps in front of it while you are fresh. Heavy enough to matter, not heavy enough to wreck the rest of your week.
Pressing is deliberately absent and pulling is not. Your shoulder already presses all week on court, so the volume goes into legs and back instead.

before.label: Not today
before.text: A sore knee, ankle, hip or lower back, or an injury in the last month? Get it looked at first.

before.label: Stop and get it checked
before.text: A sharp pain, pain that spreads or runs down a leg, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop.

before.label: Stop now
before.text: Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right. Get it looked at before you train again. Told to be careful with hard exercise? Check with your doctor first.

before.label: A day or two later
before.text: Far more sore than normal, or your pee goes dark? Get it checked the same day.

before.label: Past injury
before.text: Coming back from a knee or ankle injury? Ask whoever treated you if jumps and heavy squats are OK.

before.label: Check the setup
before.text: Set the safety arms or pins in the rack just below the bottom of your squat. No rack? Do the Goblet Squat instead. Nothing overhead for the jumps, like a fan or a low beam.

before.label: Keep clear
before.text: 48 hours away from another heavy leg session or hard running, and not the day before a match.

before.label: First time
before.text: Do two sets of each lift instead of the full sets, and see how you feel in two days.

good: Easy to moderate, any machine you like
Warm enough to sweat, not enough to tire you
bad: Going hard — you are lifting in fifteen minutes

good: Push through your heels until your hips are level
Feel the glutes, not the lower back
bad: Arching the back to lift higher

good: Back hip down first, then rotate and reach tall
Feel the front of the back hip open
bad: Rotating before the hip has opened

good: Light weight at the chest, slow, find today's depth
It should feel like a rehearsal, not a set
bad: Loading it up — this is prep

exercises.name: Empty Bar Warm-Up Sets

good: Empty bar, then two or three rising sets to your working weight
Drop the reps as the weight goes up
bad: Jumping from the empty bar to your top set

exercises.note: These do not count as working sets and carry no RPE.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump

good: Dip fast and jump as high as you can
Land soft and reset between every rep
bad: Rushing the reps and turning it into conditioning

exercises.note: Power goes first in the session, while you are fresh.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat

good: Brace before every rep, then sit between the hips
Same depth on the last rep as the first
bad: Knees caving in as it gets heavy

exercises.note: Leave two or three reps in the tank — this is not a testing day.

good: Push the hips back with the bar close to your legs
Stop where your hamstrings stop, not where the floor is
bad: Rounding the back to reach lower

good: Long stance, drop straight down, push through the front heel
The front leg does the work, not the back
bad: Leaning forward to make it easier

good: Chest on the bench, pull to the hip and pause
Feel it between the shoulder blades
bad: Heaving it with the whole body

good: Press straight out and resist the pull
Nothing should turn
bad: Letting the ribs twist towards the cable
